question: The project to build an astronomical observatory on Mount Mufara, part of Madonie Natural Park, has raised a number of concerns as to its impact on the environment and compliance with land protection rules1.

Both the size of the planned building, of a surface area of 800 m2 and an overall volume of 3 540 m3, together with the construction of a new road, would appear to breach the strict new building ban imposed by the Palermo Department of Cultural and Environmental Heritage.

Given the importance of this project both for scientific progress and for potential local economic development, it is essential to ensure that all the stages of its construction comply with current environmental legislation. In the light of the above: 1.

Can the Commission provide details of how environmental requirements will be addressed during the construction of the observatory, with a view to safeguarding the unique biodiversity and the geological features of Mount Mufara and the Madonie Natural Park?

Is the Commission aware of any procedural irregularities or shortcomings concerning the necessary authorisations, and how does it intend to ensure that the project is implemented in full compliance with EU law2?

What action is planned to facilitate a constructive dialogue between the relevant authorities and environmental associations with a view to finding a solution that strikes the right balance between scientific innovation and environmental conservation?

An appeal lodged with the Regional Administrative Court of Sicily by associations such as the Italian Alpine Club, Legambiente Sicily, Lipu and WWF cites procedural irregularities and the absence of crucial authorisations, including the lack of a favourable opinion from the Regional Council for the Protection of Natural Heritage.

The constitutional legitimacy of Article 9 of Decree-Law 104/2023, granting exemptions enabling such facilities to be built in protected areas, has also been called into question. The Administrative Court of Sicily has ordered a suspension to the project following an appeal by a number of environmental associations: the Italian Alpine Club, Legambiente Sicily, Lipu and WWF Sicily.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.12.2024) Projects to build an astronomical observatory are not listed in the Annexes of the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Directive1, but they or their associated works (such as roads) may be considered infrastructure projects2.

For such projects, Member States should determine if they are to be made subject to an assessment because of the likely significant effects on the environment taking into account the relevant selection criteria (such as size and design of the whole project, location, cumulation with other existing and/or approved projects) in Annex III of the Directive.

If the Italian authorities conclude that the project will have significant effects on the environment, an EIA has to be carried out. For projects subject to an EIA, Member States have to ensure that the public is informed and that consultations with the public concerned3 and local, regional and environmental authorities are carried out.

The Madonie natural park is designated as a Natura 2000 site, under the Habitats4 and the Birds5 Directives. Under Article 6.3 the Habitats Directive, any project likely to have a significant effect on a Natura 2000 site shall be subject to an appropriate assessment of its implications for the site in view of the site's conservation objectives.

Italy transposed the above provisions6 and has adopted appropriate national guidelines7. Sicily has also adopted specific guidelines8. The Commission is not aware of the details of the mentioned project. However, without prejudice to the Commission’s role as guardian of the Treaties, national authorities, including the judiciary, are primarily responsible to ensure compliance with the relevant EU environmental law.
It appears that judicial proceedings are currently ongoing9.
1 Directive 2011/92/EU on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the

environment, OJ L 26, 28.1.2012, as amended by Directive 2014/52/EU, OJ L 124, 25.4.2014. 2 EIA Directive, Annex II, point 10 (b) or (e). 3 Including environmental associations. 4 Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora, OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, p. 7–50. 5 Directive 2009/147/EC on the conservation of wild birds, OJ L 020 26.1.2010, p. 7.
